claims.text: On Friday 28 June 2024, in the last session before the closing of OWASP Global AppSec EU at the Lisbon Congress Centre, the owner gave Deterministic GenAI Outputs with Provenance.
claims.quote: in the last session before the closing of OWASP Global AppSec EU at the Lisbon Congress Centre

claims.text: The talk had 132 slides and a live demo.
claims.quote: OWASP Global AppSec EU; 132 slides; a live demo.

claims.text: The title was the whole argument: deterministic, GenAI, output, with provenance, meaning traceability, source tracking and documentation, lineage and origin verification.
claims.quote: Traceability, Source Tracking & Documentation, Lineage, Origin Verification

claims.text: The quiz for the room: the sixth most powerful programming language in the world is Portuguese, because data is now code and GenAI prompts are written in natural languages.
claims.quote: Since data is now code, and GenAI prompts are written in natural languages

claims.text: With 236 million first-language speakers of Portuguese, that is a lot of programmers.
claims.quote: With 236 million first-language speakers, that is a lot of programmers.

claims.text: The talk asked for models in the language: Portuguese from Portugal, Angola, Mozambique and Cape Verde.
claims.quote: we need Portuguese from Portugal, Portuguese from Angola, Portuguese from Mozambique, Portuguese from Cape Verde

claims.text: It happened for Portugal: Amália, an open model for European Portuguese built on the European EuroLLM, was released as open source in 2026 with a technical report and a pt-PT benchmark.
claims.quote: an open model for European Portuguese, built on the European EuroLLM and released as open source in 2026

claims.text: The other varieties of Portuguese are still waiting.
claims.quote: The other varieties are still waiting.

claims.text: The idea that language is the programming language is now ordinary: it is what explorer coding is.
claims.quote: it is what explorer coding is

claims.text: GenAI is the next technological revolution not because it can create content but because it can understand content.
claims.quote: Not because it can CREATE content, But because it can UNDERSTAND content

claims.text: Hallucinations are a feature when creating content and wanting creativity, but a bug and a problem when we want facts, evidence and trust.
claims.quote: But are a BUG and PROBLEM when we want facts, evident and trust

claims.text: From an attacker's point of view GenAI is your most vulnerable API, your most dangerous insider threat and a crazy black box; it is not secure, and maybe safe depending on implementation.
claims.quote: GenAI is "Your most vulnerable API", "Your most dangerous Insider Threat"

claims.text: The principles: read-only models, it is about the prompts, bring your content, assume all content and prompts are exposed, double down on AppSec and cyber.
claims.quote: Assume all content and prompts are exposed

claims.text: One slide the owner is proud of now: use graphs instead of RAG; take the content, summarise, build graphs of it, then navigate the graph.
claims.quote: you take the content, you summarize, you build graphs of it, then you navigate the graph

claims.text: Provenance is the rule of this newsroom, every claim checked against a source and linked; graphs became fractal semantic graphs and every article has one; determinism became the principle that the nearer to commodity, the fewer agents in line.
claims.quote: Provenance is the rule of this newsroom: every claim checked against a source and linked.

claims.text: What changed is the threat: in 2024 the insider was a model answering questions; in 2026 it is an agent with tools, and the answer is a behaviour policy and authority outside the model.
claims.quote: in 2026 it is an agent with tools, and the answer is a behaviour policy and authority outside the model

claims.text: The middle of the talk was a live demo of The Cyber Boardroom, built in the previous two months, open source, with every release on PyPI, Docker Hub and AWS.
claims.quote: open source, with every release on PyPI, Docker Hub and AWS

claims.text: The problem it solved was not specific to security: how to communicate with stakeholders using their language, culture, knowledge, state, interests and level of ownership.
claims.quote: how do you communicate with stakeholders using their language, culture, knowledge, state, interests, and level of ownership?

claims.text: The demo showed a board member's question answered in several languages, three board-member personas asking the same question, a fourth model reviewing the other three, and Athena, the cyber security advisor.
claims.quote: three board-member personas asking the same question, a fourth model reviewing the other three

claims.text: The shape changed since: one assistant answering questions became teams of agents doing work, each with a role, a mandate and a record.
claims.quote: one assistant answering questions became teams of agents doing work, each with a role, a mandate and a record

claims.text: The talk ended with the challenge: the future of Portugal depends on getting this right, otherwise Portugal just becomes another consumer of global technology.
claims.quote: Otherwise, Portugal just becomes another consumer of global technology

claims.text: It is the same challenge as 2010 and 2016 with a better lever: in 2010 the lever was security, in 2016 code, and in 2024 language.
claims.quote: in 2010 the lever was security, in 2016 code, and in 2024 language

claims.text: Not the first time the owner mentioned The Cyber Boardroom; it was its first live demo in Portugal that can be documented.
claims.quote: It was its first live demo in Portugal that I can document.

claims.text: Not that the talk led to Amália: many people asked for a Portuguese model.
claims.quote: Many people asked for a Portuguese model.

claims.text: The commentary is the owner's, now; the slides and transcript are from 2024.
claims.quote: The slides and transcript are from 2024.
